issues.situation: The trigger is broader than the evidence. The block treats X as short when obj_oc_remaining[X] > 0. That number includes COORD-5's projected enemy OC (PROJECTED_NEED_CAP 4 x per-model scale, about 12-16 OC for the bench armies). The block also never checks that no other unit is assigned to X, although its note and print say 'no other unit joins it'. So it also fires on captures that flip X now and are short only against a possible enemy counter-move, and on an X that other units also go to. Concrete case, from a V10 full game (Orks-mirror reserve-fixture smoke run, seed 92001, /root/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/40k/logs/debug_20261031_034853.log, R4 P1 plan near line 47879, cards near lines 48491 and 48714). Warbikers Beta and Alpha (6 OC each) Advance to obj_nml_2, which the enemy holds with 3 OC. 12 vs 3 is a flip, but the plan reads 'needs 10/4 more OC' because of projected OC. Both cards rank Move obj_center first (42.5/41.7 vs 20.0/19.4). The centre is 'flipping it (enemy holds with OC 3)' and is already covered by the Stompa (12 OC) with Wazdakka holding, and 3 more units go there as support. The block redirects Beta, which re-opens obj_nml_2's need, so Alpha qualifies too. obj_nml_2 is left to the enemy and the over-covered centre gets 2 more units. In R3 P2 of the same game, Warbikers Alpha joins the Stompa on obj_nml_1 (18 OC vs 10) and would be pulled to the centre. With fast M12 armies nearly every objective carries projected OC, so this is the normal firing shape in the Orks fixtures. It is not the evidence shape (s7475/s7455: 9 OC alone vs 11, no flip possible).
issues.proposed_change: In the block, skip (continue) unless the trip is both futile now and alone. (a) The plan's OC on X must be <= eval enemy_oc at X, where plan OC = eval friendly_oc + incoming_oc[X] + unit_oc of every assignment to X with action hold/move/advance, this unit included. (b) No other assignment may target X; this makes the note true and stops the double redirect. Optional (c): skip when Y's planned OC already exceeds enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc at Y by at least this unit's OC, because the extra unit no longer matters there. Both findings still fire (9 vs 11, alone). Add unit tests for a projection-only shortfall and for a co-assigned X.

- Small and isolated. It is param-gated (FIX_ATTACK_MOVE=0 gives the base exactly) and placed after pass 2.5 and the backfill. It does not touch the chase gate, and none of the V12 hunks (WAAAGH-ADV-CHARGE, R1-HOME-LAST) overlap its insertion point, so it should rebase cleanly.

reviews.summary:
The narrow design redirects a short capture to the unit's top-scored enemy-held objective that friends already cover. Its core gate is sensible: it separates the two clear round-2 findings from look-alikes where our own centre made the extra unit harmful or neutral.

The trigger is broader than its evidence, though. "Short" includes COORD-5's projected enemy OC (about 12-16 OC here), and the "nobody joins" check the note promises is never coded. So in fast-army games it pulls units off flips that succeed now. In a V10 Orks-mirror game it would move two Warbikers squads (12 OC) off an objective held by 3 enemy OC, onto a centre already covered by the Stompa. That is the common firing shape in the Orks fixtures, and it is likely worse play.

Fix: require plan OC on the target <= current enemy OC and no co-assigned unit, and optionally stop stacking on a centre with ample surplus.

Even after that, it is a weak ship candidate:
- It never fired in the designer's 6 Custodes-mirror bench games, and limited to its evidence shape it probably fails the v2 reach gate.
- Its base-measured finding s7475 r2 flips sign at horizon 2 (-3.00).
- s7455 r2 has no horizon-2 check.
- It misses the cluster's only horizon-2-confirmed finding, s7421 r2 (+14.83).

Revise, re-check s7455 r2 at horizon 2, then run the v2 fix gate, and park it if reach stays below 1.0 line per game. Evidence: /root/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/40k/logs/debug_20261031_034853.log; scan script /tmp/review_scripts/trigger_scan.py.

issues.situation: The trigger's 'short' test is `obj_oc_remaining[am_oid] > 0`. That need comes from `_initial_objective_oc_needs`: max(1, enemy_oc - friendly_oc + 1) plus COORD-5's projected enemy OC, capped at PROJECTED_NEED_CAP 4 x the army per-model scale (about 15 OC in the Custodes bench). The source gate only excludes home and held objectives, so uncontrolled and contested objectives also qualify. Result: ATTACK-MOVE redirects trips that (a) capture an uncontrolled objective this turn (oc_needed = 1, short only against the enemy's next move), (b) tie the holder (11e 14.02: equal level of control means nobody controls it, which denies the enemy), or (c) flip it now but not against the projected reinforcement. In the bench Custodes mirror, a 10-OC Guard squad moving onto a 10-OC holder is 'short 1', i.e. exactly a tie. The comment and the report both say 'the unit cannot take it and nobody joins it'; the code does not test that. Redirecting real captures and denials to stack on a covered objective is the FAR-TRIP/OVERCOMMIT failure pattern, and it is unmeasured.
issues.proposed_change: Test the current-control shortfall, not the plan need. Compute plan_oc = int(am_eval.friendly_oc) + the sum of unit_oc over capture assignments (move/advance) whose objective_id == am_oid, then require plan_oc < int(am_eval.enemy_oc): strictly below the enemy now, so neither a flip nor a tie. This also drops uncontrolled sources (enemy_oc 0). Both fire sites still qualify on the plan's own numbers (9 < 11).

issues.situation: The mechanism claim is false at both fire sites. At s7475 Alpha carries Blade Champion B; at s7455 Beta carries Blade Champion C. MovementPhase moves the attached character with the squad, but `_unit_alive_oc` counts only the bodyguard (9 OC). Each trip therefore really brings 11 OC against the holder's 11 (Guard 9 + Blade Champion 2): a tie that removes enemy control, not 'a lone 9-OC trip that changes nothing'. On top of that, s7475 r2 does not hold at horizon 2 (-3.00 [-9.10, 3.10]). s7455 r2 has not been re-checked. The cluster's only horizon-2-confirmed finding, s7421 r2 (+14.83), cannot be reached by construction: its source objective obj_nml_2 is held by us (P1 6 OC at the save), and held sources are excluded.
issues.proposed_change: Correct the rationale in the const comment and the report. If 'cannot change control' is meant literally, add attached characters' OC (attachment_data.attached_characters) to plan_oc. That stops the rule firing at both findings, which shows the predicate is not the mechanism the rollouts measured (denial on the centre). Weigh the design on s7455 r2 alone until it is horizon-2 checked.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Measured: 0 lines in 6 Custodes-mirror games, with every pair identical to base, which independently confirms nothing fired. My estimate from the trigger conditions: about 0-0.2 per game in the Custodes mirror, about 0.1-0.5 in asym, about 0-0.3 in the Orks mirror. Pooled that is well under the 1.0/game V2-1 fix gate. Reason: in one movement plan (built once per phase, so lines roughly equal redirects) the rule needs a capture move/advance still short after pass 2.5 and backfill, AND that unit's top-scored candidate to be a different move/advance objective that is enemy-held or contested, fully covered (remaining 0), with a friend hold/move/advance assigned there, no slower, and passing TOO-LATE/RACE-SKIP. In the bench (no reserves, no attached leaders, P1 first), P1's round 1 has no enemy-held objective at all (P1 moves first). Later, covering an enemy-held objective means meeting enemy OC + 1 + COORD-5 projected extra (up to about 15 OC for the Custodes bench army), which takes 2-4 squads. Pass-2.5 attack conversions re-open needs, and OBJ-BACKFILL-1 already moves short-trip units back onto them. The designer's near-miss diagnostic found the 'short capture' shape about 2 times per game, but each was blocked because the top was uncontrolled or was the unit's own objective. Orks: big holder OC (Gretchin 22, Stompa 12, Deffkoptas 12) makes 'covered' rare, and aggression converts many captures to attacks, which the rule skips. Asym, P1 Custodes against a small Ork holder in rounds 2-3, is the most likely place to see an occasional fire.
reviews.strengths: Small, fully gated block. Param 0 gives base decisions exactly; the only side effect is a _param_reads bookkeeping entry. It reuses apply_capture_assignment, too_late and race_hopeless, and re-opens the abandoned objective's consumed OC correctly (the redirected unit consumes 0 at the covered top, so nothing is double counted). It iterates a keys() copy, so erase and re-insert is safe. Cost is negligible: O(assignments x candidates) once per movement phase. It adds an [ATTACK_MOVE] log line and a coordination_note narrated at execution; no debug logs removed. It runs after the chase gate, but for a move/advance the gate's verdict does not depend on the objective unless the unit stands on it. So the redirected Normal move goes through the same execution path as the rollout's forced branch B, and the mode is the candidate's own. It skips 'attack' assignments, so it is orthogonal to the V12 waaagh chase-gate change; the patch applies cleanly on 12e0753 and on top of the V12 patch. The enemy-held top gate does separate some measured twins: s7413 r2 (harmful) has a centre we hold, 11-0, and is blocked, while s7475 r2 and s7455 r2 (clear) have an enemy-held centre (P2 3 and 14 OC in the hosting area) and fire. The report's finding and guardrail claims match what the code would do. The main test fails on base for the right reason through the real planner.
reviews.summary: I recommend dropping this design. The code itself is careful and exactly gated, and the patch applies cleanly on 12e0753 and on top of the V12 waaagh patch. The problems are with the rule and its evidence. First, its 'short' test is the plan's need, which includes COORD-5 projected enemy OC and the +1 for a strict majority, and it also admits uncontrolled source objectives. So it can redirect trips that capture, flip or tie the objective now (under 14.02 a tie denies the enemy). That contradicts its own rationale. The concrete fix is to require plan OC below the enemy OC now. Second, the mechanism claim is wrong at both fire sites: the attached Blade Champion makes each trip 11 OC against 11, a tie. Third, the evidence is thin: s7475 r2, its main fire site, fades at horizon 2 (-3.00); the cluster's only horizon-2-confirmed finding, s7421 r2 (+14.83), cannot be reached by construction; and the closest harmful twin, s7411 r3 P1 (-2.25), may also trigger and was not replayed. Fourth, it fired 0 times in 6 bench games, and its trigger conditions keep it well under the 1.0 per game V2-1 gate on all three fixtures, so it would be parked. The only way to raise reach, allowing uncontrolled tops, repeats the FAR-TRIP/OVERCOMMIT failure pattern from round 2. I could not run Godot (read-only brief), so the designer's replay results and test pass counts were checked against the code and the saved positions, not re-run. The firing rates for the Orks fixtures are estimates.

issues.situation:
The fix splits group trips and creates the short capture it is meant to remove. Help counts only unassigned units that arrive no later than the unit being placed (`h.turns_to_reach <= c.turns_to_reach`). Units already sent to the same objective are never looked at again, and OBJ-ASSIGN-1 'closer' assignments skip the check entirely. These sites are traced from the V10 reach records in test_results/fx10_reach (per-unit candidate lists, rounds 1-3); they were not replayed.
- asym_2000 R1 P1 (Custodes): 4 Custodian Guard (40 OC) advance on the Ork home. Need is 39 including projection, so the group fills it. Guard Alpha is visited first (3 turns). The other three are 4 turns out, so help = 2 OC (one Blade Champion) vs gap 29. Alpha is sent to the centre, where Gamma plus 3 support units are already going and the Orks race about 60 OC. The remaining 3 Guard continue 9 OC short.
- mirror_orks R2 P1: OBJ-ASSIGN-1 sends Warbikers Beta to the enemy home first. Warbikers Alpha is then redirected (gap 21 vs help 17 from Mek, Wartrikes and Stormboyz). Beta walks on alone, 6 OC vs 18.
These are the only bench fires I could find, so this is mostly how the fix would act in the bench.
issues.proposed_change:
Decide per objective, not per unit.
- Before redirecting, add up the OC already assigned to X plus the OC of unassigned units that pass 2 could send there within the group's arrival window (the slowest assigned unit's turns, or c.turns+1). If that meets the need, keep the unit.
- If it does not, re-route every unit assigned to X that has a covered, contested top-up, OBJ-ASSIGN-1 closers included. Then close X for the rest of pass 2 and for the COORD-4 backfill.
- Run the same test on the OBJ-ASSIGN-1 closer before applying it.

issues.situation: Round 4-5 time limit. The top-up target is not checked by TOO-LATE or RACE-SKIP. `max(2, c.turns)` lets a 1-turn short capture be swapped for a 2-turn top-up, and MOVE_REACH_HORIZON is 0, so the top-up's score is not cut. In battle round 5 the unit gives up a capture it reaches now, which can still tie (deny) or contest, for an objective it reaches after the game ends.
issues.proposed_change: Apply too_late and race_hopeless to the top-up candidate, and require battle_round + top.turns - 1 <= MAX_BATTLE_ROUNDS_AI (or top.turns <= c.turns in rounds 4-5).

issues.situation: The top-up's OC is invisible to the ledger (oc_consumed 0). When a unit already assigned to the top objective converts to ATTACK in pass 2.5 (common for melee Custodes and Orks), the COORD-4 backfill re-fills the re-opened need with another unit or an OBJ-BACKFILL-1 switch, even though the top-up unit is already heading there. That stacks the centre further; in both reconstructed bench fires the centre already had 3-4 units committed by the support pass.
issues.proposed_change: Keep a per-objective tally of top-up OC and subtract it from any need re-opened in pass 2.5 before the backfill runs.

Price both options instead of overriding:
- top-up = top VP x P(enemy flips it without this unit);
- short trip = c VP x P(the plan reaches the need in time) + denial when our OC reaches a tie with the live enemy OC.
At minimum, measure the gap against the live-control need, or require the projected units to be 'nearest' to c.

  - Orks mirror (ork_94002): 1 site, R2 P1 Warbikers Alpha, gap 21 vs help 17.
  - Asym (asy_99002): 1 site, R1 P1 Custodian Guard Alpha, gap 29 vs help 2. It depends on the seed's cards but recurs whenever the candidate plays Custodes P1 with that plan.
- **Rate:** about 2 fires in 18 movement phases, about 0.11 per phase. That gives about 0.55 per game over the candidate's 5 phases: Custodes about 0, Orks and asym about 0.5-1 per game. Rounds 4-5 were not observed; fewer surviving units means less help, which could raise the rate.
- **Where it fires:** both reconstructed fires are group trips to the enemy home objective, not the lone side-objective flips of the findings.
reviews.strengths:
- **Safe gating:** small and param-gated. FIX_ATTACK_MOVE=0 restores the base path exactly. It adds a tag, a narrated reason and a coordination note.
- **Placement:** it runs after every existing pass-2 filter, so it never overrides DIM-RETURNS, TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP or LONE-TRIP on the short capture.
- **V12 compatibility:** it leaves the melee chase gate and charge-intent blending alone, so it is semantically compatible with V12's waaagh fix.
- **Conservative trigger:** the help count is generous and enemy pressure is required on the top-up. That keeps quiet top-ups out and, by about 1 inch of projection range, also the harmful s7413 r2 P1.
- **Designer's checks:** it changes all three finding decisions and none of the five guardrails. The unit test fails on base and passes on the fix, and the related suites pass.
- **Real target:** it addresses a genuine ledger flaw. Pass 2 scores a capture that leaves its objective short as if the unit took the objective.
reviews.summary:
**Verdict: revise.** Root's rule makes a unit top up its covered, contested best objective when its move/advance capture leaves the target short and no unassigned unit can close the gap in time. The idea is reasonable. Over full games, though, it would act mostly where there is no evidence, and in an inconsistent way.

- **Group splitting:** help only counts units that arrive no later than the unit being placed, and units already sent (including OBJ-ASSIGN-1 closers) are never looked at again. In the bench sites I traced, it pulls the lead Guard out of a 4-Guard advance on the Ork home that fills the need. In the Orks mirror it leaves one Warbikers alone on an enemy-home trip. Either way it creates the short capture it is meant to remove.
- **Reach:** in the Custodes mirror, the fixture closest to the findings, unattached Blade Champions and screening units count as help, so it almost never fires. Pooled reach looks like about 0.3-0.8 lines per game, below the gate.
- **Evidence:** thinner than reported.
  - f1 reverses at horizon 2 (-3.00, and the top-up branch loses about 279 points more material).
  - f3 was measured as an Advance; root makes a Normal move and also redirects a second unit.
  - The same-shape s7413 r2 P1 is harmful and is avoided only by about 1 inch of projection range.
  - s7411 r3 P1 (harmful) may trigger.
- **Changes needed:**
  - decide per objective (help over the group's arrival window; keep or re-route the whole group; check closers);
  - count only help that pass 2 would really send;
  - limit scope to lone trips and round 2;
  - filter the top-up with TOO-LATE.
  Then re-measure reach and replay s7411 and s7413 before any bench.

I did not run Godot. The bench fire figures are traced from the V10 reach records, not replayed.

issues.situation: f3 (s7421 r2 P1) is the only finding confirmed at horizon 2, and there the fix does not make the move the report claims. The redirect gives Guard Gamma a Normal move to obj_center, but the unit keeps its T7-23 charge intent on Scout Squad Alpha (17.4" away, inside M8+12"). The Normal-move executor (12e0753 AIDecisionMaker.gd ~7375-7391) then aims at 0.7*charge target + 0.3*objective. From the save, the 8" move ends near (452,1345): 11.3" from obj_center and 5.3" from obj_nml_2, so it is out of control range of both. The base's own blended move ends 2.9" from obj_nml_2, inside range. The measured +9.81 (h1) and +14.83 (h2) branch was an Advance, and the Advance executor (~7089) does not blend: it ends 6.5" from the centre on an average roll and in range on a 5+. So at f3 the executed move matches none of the base, the measured branch or a top-up. The report's 'same unit and objective, only the mode differs' does not hold. The report also shows Guard Beta redirected in the same replay, which no measurement covers. I computed this from the save and the executor code; I did not run it. f1 and f2 are not affected because their charge targets are 21.4" and 20.4" away, beyond the 20" blend limit.
issues.proposed_change: Only the fix path should change, so param 0 stays exact and the chase gate is untouched. Pick one: (a) mark the redirected assignment (assignments[uid]['attack_move_topup'] = true) and skip the T7-23 blend for a marked unit whose charge target is not within 12" of the top-up objective; or (b) skip the redirect when the unit's charge target is within M+12" and nearer the abandoned objective. Then, before any bench, re-measure the fix's real plan at f3 at horizon 2: Guard C's Normal move plus the Guard B redirect.

issues.situation: The fix very likely fires at s7411 r3 P1, a position of the same shape that was measured harmful and that the report does not check. Guard Beta's best candidate is obj_center (9.5", 1 turn). Blade Champion B's hold and the others cover it, and Guard Alpha_P2 (6 OC) stands in range, so the pressure check passes. The chosen obj_nml_2 flip is short by 9 and takes 3 turns. No other P1 unit reaches obj_nml_2 within 3 turns, so help is 0. The redirect is therefore the measured 'Move obj_center' branch: -2.25 [-4.26, -0.24], n12, measured on older code. Its charge target sits at the centre, so the blend points the same way and the move is the measured one. With f1 at -3.00 at horizon 2 and the f4 Prosecutors fire unmeasured, the only evidence for the fix's real action is f2 at horizon 1 (+5.92).
issues.proposed_change: Replay s7411 r3 P1 and the other same-shape positions in measured_positions.json (s7432 r2/r3 P1, s7452 r2 P1, s7479 r2 P1, s7480 r2 P1) on 12e0753+fix. Report which ones fire and add those as guardrails. Re-check f2 at horizon 2.

issues.situation: test_help_in_time_keeps_the_flip never reaches the help branch. 'helper' is 2 turns from obj_side and outscores 'second' (3 turns), so it is assigned first. 'second' then has gap <= 0 and is kept anyway. The `>= 1` assertion is also satisfied by the helper alone. Deleting the help check therefore leaves all 5 tests passing. The turn-limit guard, which the report credits for keeping g4, and the 'covered best is a hold' exclusion are not tested either.
issues.proposed_change: Rebuild the case so 'second' reaches obj_side before the helper: put the helper at the same number of turns with a lower score. Assert that 'second' goes to obj_side with no ATTACK-MOVE coordination note. Add a case where the covered best is 3 turns away and the short capture is at most 2 turns away, and assert no redirect.

issues.situation: The gap is the ledger need minus the unit's OC, and the ledger need includes COORD-5's projected enemy OC. That projection is capped at 4 x the army's per-model scale: about 10 OC for the sweep list and about 15 for the bench Custodes list. So the fix also drops captures that would control the objective at the end of the turn. At f3 no enemy is in range of obj_nml_2; 'needs 2 more' is all projection, which contradicts the root cause's 'controls nothing'. It can also redirect reinforcements of held_threatened objectives we already control. It counts projections in the game's final turn, when the enemy has no move left. No guardrail covers a reinforcement of a held objective.
issues.proposed_change: Return {} when c's objective is held_safe or held_threatened, and ignore the projected part of the need when the enemy has no later turn. Decide on purpose whether uncontrolled, projection-only cases stay in scope (f3 is one), and say so in the report.

issues.situation: Home objectives are not exempt. DIM-RETURNS, LONE-TRIP and FAR-TRIP all say 'home is never skipped'. ATTACK-MOVE can pull a unit off capturing an uncontrolled home objective that is short only against a fast enemy's projected OC, if its covered best is the contested centre.
issues.proposed_change: In attack_move_topup, return {} when c's objective eval has is_home.

issues.situation: The decision is made per unit, which can strand units already sent to c's objective. The OBJ-ASSIGN-1 'closer' unit, or an earlier unit whose own help check counted this unit, stays on a capture that by the fix's own rule controls nothing, now with less OC. Base would at least have sent both. Also, when OBJ-ASSIGN-1 covers an objective, the unit falls through via `continue` without being recorded in am_covered_best. The top-up then targets a lower covered objective than the one the unit was displaced from.
issues.proposed_change: Skip the redirect when another unit of this plan is already assigned to c's objective. Record am_covered_best[uid] = cand in the OBJ-ASSIGN-1 'covered' fall-through.

issues.situation: The top-up candidate is recorded in the remaining<=0 branch, before pass 2's TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP, LONE-TRIP and DIM-RETURNS filters, so none of them ever checks it. In rounds 4-5 a 2-turn top-up can arrive after the game ends. The reach-horizon floor makes this unlikely because the scores are compared, but nothing rules it out.
issues.proposed_change: In attack_move_topup, return {} when too_late.call(top), race_hopeless.call(top) or lone_trip.call(top) is true.

issues.situation: Narration only. When the first covered candidate differs from blocked_best's objective, the COORD-2 loop (~11132) overwrites the ATTACK-MOVE coordination_note. The decision card then says '<X> is already covered (... en route) - redirecting to <top-up objective>'.
issues.proposed_change: In the blocked_best loop, skip units whose assignment carries the ATTACK-MOVE flag or note.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Low, and likely below the v2 fix gate (pooled >= 1.0 line per game over 6 games, so at least 6 lines). COORD-4 builds the plan once per movement phase, so the fix's seat gets about 5 chances per game. Reaching 1.0 per game needs a fire in about 20% of plans.

Custodes mirror: the designer measured 0 lines in 2 games, and the two games were identical. The bench Custodes list differs from the sweep list the findings came from:
- Bench: 6 Guard units of 5 models at OC2 (10 OC, M6), Allarus 15 OC, 3 Blade Champions at OC2, no reserves.
- Sweeps: 4 Guard units of 3 models at OC3 (9 OC, M8), with reserves.
So the 9-against-11-OC pattern rarely recurs, and the Blade Champions can cover gaps of 1-3 as help. In P1's round 1 no P2 unit is within one move of the centre (11.8"), so the pressure check fails.

Orks mirror: 17 units, mostly M12, so help within the same number of turns usually covers the gap. Estimate about 0-0.3 per game.

Custodes vs Orks: the likeliest source. The Custodes seat faces fast Orks, so projected needs reach the ~15 OC cap and the M5-6 helpers are slow. Estimate about 0.3-1 per Custodes-seat game.

Pooled estimate: about 0.2-0.6 lines per game. To pass, the 4 unmeasured asym and Orks games would need at least 6 lines.

The reach run's high attack_move count (44 per game) is 'moving toward charge target' and 'advances to attack' text, which this design neither targets nor changes. Expected bench effect is under 0.5 fires per game times about +0.5-1 VP per fire (the same-shape positions average about +0.4-0.7). That is far below what the sequential bench can detect.
reviews.strengths:
- The diagnosis is sharp: the pass-2 ledger gives zero value to OC past an objective's need, but still gives a capture that leaves the objective short its full candidate score.
- The change is small and confined to pass 2 of _assign_units_to_objectives.
- FIX_ATTACK_MOVE=0 restores the base exactly. All new state sits behind attack_move_on: am_covered_best is never filled and the helper returns {} first, so apply_capture_assignment(cand) runs as before. The only side effect is a get_param read record.
- No null or empty access problems: all candidate keys exist and top_ev.is_empty() is checked. No dead or reserve units are involved, since candidates are only alive, deployed, movable units. No double count: help sums one candidate per unit and objective.
- Cheap: at most one O(candidates) loop per unit per plan, and the plan is built once per phase.
- It is not a veto. A redirected unit still goes forward to a contested objective, so it avoids the 'units held back' failure of FAR_TRIP and OVERCOMMIT.
- The help, pressure and turn-limit guards are sensible. The pressure guard correctly excludes s7413 r2 P1, a same-shape position measured harmful (-4.58 [-8.22, -0.95]), whose centre had no enemy within one move.
- The [ATTACK_MOVE] log line gives gap, help, scores and turns, and a coordination note is added. No debug log is removed. Style matches the neighbouring fixes.
- It leaves the chase gate alone. On a temporary copy of the shipped V12 tree (1.56.8), the patch applies with fuzz and its hunks land in the right places, after the R1-HOME-LAST helpers.
- The test drives the real planner (_evaluate_all_objectives and _assign_units_to_objectives). It pins the param on, tests param 0, erases the override, and fails on base for the right reason: base sends 'second' alone to obj_side.
- The report's geometry for f1 and f2, and the turn-limit claim for g4, check out against the saves.
reviews.summary:
Verdict: revise. As code, the patch is correct, contained, gated, cheap and compatible with V12. The test pins the redirect and fails on base for the right reason.

Major issue: the redirect ignores the unit's T7-23 charge intent. At f3 (s7421 r2 P1), the only finding confirmed at horizon 2, Guard Gamma's Normal 'top-up' move is blended 70% toward Scout Squad Alpha. It ends about 5.3" from obj_nml_2 and 11.3" from obj_center, so it neither takes nml_2 (base ended 2.9" from it) nor tops up the centre. The measured +9.81 / +14.83 branch was an Advance, which does not blend. I computed this from the save and the executor code; I did not run it.

What is left of the evidence:
- f1 flips sign at horizon 2 (-3.00).
- The trigger very likely fires at s7411 r3 P1, which was measured harmful (-2.25 [-4.26, -0.24]).
- The extra fires in the f3 and f4 replays are unmeasured.
- That leaves f2 at horizon 1 (+5.92) as the only support for the action as built.

Minor issues:
- Test 2 never exercises the help branch, and the turn-limit guard is untested.
- The gap counts projected enemy OC, so captures that would hold at the end of the turn are dropped too (f3 is one), as are reinforcements of objectives we already hold.
- Home objectives are not exempt, unlike DIM-RETURNS, LONE-TRIP and FAR-TRIP.
- Units already sent to the short objective can be stranded, and the OBJ-ASSIGN-1 fall-through is not recorded.
- The top-up is never checked by the TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP or LONE-TRIP filters.
- The COORD-2 note can overwrite the new coordination note.

Bench reach is the binding problem. It was measured at 0 in the Custodes pair and I estimate about 0.2-0.6 lines per game pooled. Unless the Custodes vs Orks and Orks pairs fire a lot, protocol v2's fix gate parks it even after the revision.

Files: /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/.ai_lab_work/wt_panel_am/tools/ai_lab/r5_designs/attack_move/root.patch and root.json. The executor references are 12e0753 40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd ~7089 (Advance, no blend) and ~7375-7391 (T7-23 blend).

issues.situation: The core case does not hold past one round, and the design misses the cluster's only robust finding. Situation: Custodes mirror, round 2, P1. A 3-model Custodian Guard unit (OC 9) is 13-18" from the centre, and the capped COORD-5 need there is already filled. The base walks the unit toward an enemy-held flank NML objective it is trying to flip. The fix sends it on a 2-move trip to the centre. By the planner's own turns_to_reach the gaps are 9.5", 14.1" and 11.2" against M8 at s7475, s7455 and s7454. (1) s7475 r2 P1: the fix reproduces the measured alternative exactly, but the gain flips sign once round 4 is included (+4.00 [1.04, 6.96] at h1, -3.00 [-9.10, 3.10] at h2). Round 4 is the first Command phase where a round-3 arrival at the centre can score for P1. (2) s7454 r3 P2: the base has drifted (V10 sends Gamma toward P2's own home, obj_home_2). The fix redirects Gamma from that home objective to the centre. The centre alternative measured -3.42 [-9.62, 2.78] at h2, and the fix uses a Normal move where the measured alternative was an Advance. (3) s7455 r2 has not been re-checked at h2. (4) The only finding confirmed at h2, s7421 r2 P1 (+14.83 [7.13, 22.53]), is not reached. The designer's own A/B shows its value was denying the opponent's centre scoring; the share-of-worst-case-threat test cannot see that (18 vs 25 = 0.72 < 0.75). (5) Two positions with the same pattern were measured harmful and not replayed: s7413 r2 P1 (Guard Alpha flipping obj_nml_2 -> Move obj_center, -4.58 [-8.22, -0.95]) and s7411 r3 P1 (Guard Beta flipping obj_nml_2, enemy OC 17 -> Move obj_center, -2.25 [-4.26, -0.24]).
issues.proposed_change: Do not bench on this evidence. If the idea is retried: (a) run an h2 rollout of the fix's own whole-plan decision at s7455 r2 P1; (b) replay s7413 r2 P1 and s7411 r3 P1 with the fix and narrow the trigger if it fires there; (c) require the unit to actually flip the top by the plan's own measure, tp.ours > tp.threat (ATTACK_MOVE_MIN_SHARE >= 1.0). The [ATTACK_MOVE] line already claims 'its OC keeps control there', but shares of 0.75-0.99 still lose. A denial trigger is a separate design aimed at s7421: the top is reachable this turn (Advance included), the enemy holds it now, and our OC there with the unit >= the enemy OC there now.

issues.situation: Neither bench fire matches the cluster's pattern, and the only full-game pair is -24, all from those fires. The pair is Custodes mirror, seed 93101. In M1 (fix in the P2 seat) the fix fired 0 times. A fix that never fires gives identical games (V9 keeper: 64/64), so M1 is the base-vs-base game: P1 won by 53. In M2 (fix as P1) it fired twice and P1 won by only 5, so E = -24 comes entirely from those two redirects. That is n=1 and high variance, but it is causal and it is the only full-game data. Fire (a): 'Allarus Custodians -> obj_center instead of obj_home_2'. For P1 that fallback is the ENEMY home. Six of the 11e primary cards pay hold_enemy_home: Vital Link 10 eog, Vanguard Operation 10 eog, Punishment 8 eog, Inescapable Dominion 5 eog, Meatgrinder 5 eot rounds 2-5, Outmanoeuvre 10 eot. Behind Enemy Lines also pays 3 per unit wholly in the enemy deployment zone. eot and eog scoring does not depend on the one-move projected enemy OC that the futility test uses. Fire (b): 'Guard Beta -> obj_nml_2 instead of obj_center'. This pulled a unit OFF the centre, the reverse of every clear finding in the cluster. In a mirror the centre is almost always 'futile' under the worst-case projection, so a flank top often looks better. In the s7454 replay the fix also redirected P2's Gamma away from its own home objective (h2 -3.42).
issues.proposed_change: Allow the redirect only when the top is the central objective (all 4 clear findings are centre-instead-of-flank). Never allow it when the fallback is is_home or is_enemy_home: an enemy holding our home pays them hold_enemy_home, and the enemy home pays us on those cards. Then re-run the V2-1 reach with 1 pair on each of the 3 fixtures before any bench. Under these limits the one measured pair would have had 0 fires, so expect reach to fall; park the fix if it is below 1.0 per game.

issues.situation: The fallback-futility test is a broader copy of FAR_TRIP's skip, which already lost in this fixture. Situation: Custodes mirror, rounds 2-4. A Guard squad's next option is an enemy-held or contested flank objective, often still 'needing N more OC after this unit'. The test is fb_futile = fb.ours <= fb.threat. ours counts only holders, units already placed EARLIER in the greedy order, and this unit. It leaves out units that will join later and units that can reach the objective in time (RACE-ARMY's 'army', which lone_trip_oc already returns). A tie counts as futile, and any trip length qualifies. The threat counts every enemy unit within M+2" of the flank, even when the same units are also counted in the centre's threat. FAR_TRIP skipped only a subset of these trips (2+ moves, help < own OC, threat > near). FAR_TRIP + OVERCOMMIT lost -6.26 VP/game [-9.71, -2.81] over 42 pairs in this same mirror (+7.8 in the Orks mirror), because units kept off flank trips scored less on cards that need units across the table. Sending the unit 'forward' to the centre does not fix that. Engage on All Fronts ignores units within 6" of the centre, Outflank needs units within 6" of an edge, and Secure No Man's Land needs 2 NML objectives. The redirect also leaves the fallback's need open. Where the unit filled that need in the base, a later, weaker unit can now be sent there alone (s7455: 'flipping it (enemy holds with OC 11) — worth ~3 VP', no need left).
issues.proposed_change: If the idea is retried: (a) judge the fallback army against army with a strict test (lone_trip_oc's army < threat, the RACE-SKIP/LONE-TRIP standard), and only for trips of 2+ moves the unit would make alone (FAR_TRIP's help < own OC); (b) limit the trigger to battle rounds 2-3, which covers all the evidence; (c) when it fires, keep later pass-2 units out of that fallback when their OC also leaves it futile, so the redirect does not swap in a weaker lone unit. These limits will remove most fires.

issues.situation: The cluster's 'attack move' is the T7-23 execution blend: 70% toward the charge target when it is within M+12". The design leaves the blend on. For a redirected Guard unit with such a charge intent, only the 30% objective share of its move target changes. The 'with the unit' OC counted at the top therefore assumes an arrival that the blend can prevent turn after turn. The decision checks do not show where redirected units actually ended up; the fix_choice texts drop the 'moving toward charge target' wording that execution prints.
issues.proposed_change: Redirect (and count the unit at the top) only when the unit has no in-range charge intent, or when its charge target lies toward the top (alignment > 0.5, the test T7-23's charge_lane term already uses). Report end positions in the decision checks.

issues.situation: There is no round limit. TOO-LATE blocks only 2-move tops in round 5. From round 4 on, the worst-case one-move projection is a poor proxy: P1's round-5 move has no later P1 Command phase, and eot/eog cards (hold_enemy_home, eot hold_central, Behind Enemy Lines, Outflank, Engage on All Fronts) pay for positions the test ignores. With MIN_SHARE 0.75 the plan can still lose the centre, and the redirected unit then scores nowhere.
issues.proposed_change: Limit the trigger to battle rounds 2-3 (or at most <= 4), the window that holds the evidence.

issues.situation: Code hygiene. ATTACK_MOVE_MAX_TURNS is a plain const, not read through get_param, so a bench profile cannot sweep it. The [ATTACK_MOVE] text says 'its OC keeps control there' even at shares of 0.75-0.99. The top is not re-checked against DIM-RETURNS (reprice_capture(top).skip). The check is not applied in the COORD-4 backfill or the OBJ-ASSIGN-1 'closer' paths, so units placed there can still go to futile fallbacks. The hunk sits right next to V12's R1-HOME-LAST insertion after the pass-2 loop, so the rebase needs a trivial manual merge (no conflict with the chase gate).
issues.proposed_change: Read MAX_TURNS through get_param. Word the log line by share: 'flips/keeps control' when >= 1.0, otherwise 'closer contest'. Add the reprice_capture skip to the top checks. Either apply the check in the backfill and closer paths or document why it is not applied there.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Estimate: about 0.6-0.9 [ATTACK_MOVE] lines per game with the fix in one seat, pooled over the 3 fixtures. That is borderline against the V2-1 fix gate (>= 1.0). The plan is built once per Movement phase (COORD-4), so one line is roughly one changed decision. Per fixture: (1) Custodes mirror, about 1 per game. Measured: 2 fires in the designer's one pair, both in the P1 seat and 0 as P2. Moving second, the centre is usually already enemy-held and the share stays under 0.75. (2) Custodes vs Orks, about 0.5-1 per game. The s7418 r3 replay of this matchup fired for both sides (Warbikers A -> centre, Guard Delta -> obj_nml_1). But Ork mobs often keep the Custodes' centre share below 0.75, or out-OC the threat without the extra unit. (3) Orks mirror, about 0.3-0.7 per game. This is a guess with no replay: large per-model OC scales the COORD-5 cap up (4 x the army's per-model scale), so a top that is 'filled but still out-OC'd' is rarer. Quality of the fires: only about half are the pattern the evidence covers (Guard -> centre instead of a flank flip), and in the one measured pair 0 of 2 were. Under the limits in issue 2 (centre top only, no home or enemy-home fallback) that pair would have had 0 fires, so a narrowed version probably fails the reach gate.
reviews.strengths:
- Clean gate: with FIX_ATTACK_MOVE at 0 the lambda returns {} before doing any work, and the check is read-only (lookups and logs), so a game where it never fires is identical to base. M1 of its bench pair shows this.
- One small insertion point at the end of the pass-2 loop.
- The redirect keeps the top candidate's own action, so a Normal move stays a Normal move.
- It refuses home tops, tops more than 2 moves away, and TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP or LONE-TRIP tops.
- It limits itself: a redirected unit uses up no need and is counted in 'ours', so once the plan out-OCs the threat the next unit is not pivotal.
- It always sends units forward, never back to our home, which answers the 'held back' half of the round-2 lesson.
- It does not touch _melee_chase_gate or the T7-23 blend, so it works alongside V12's waaagh_advance_charge change. Only a trivial textual merge next to V12's R1-HOME-LAST hunk is needed.
- Good diagnostics: [ATTACK_MOVE_CHECK] logs every number, [ATTACK_MOVE] logs each change, and the decision card gets a coordination note.
- The failing-first unit test drives _assign_units_to_objectives with real evaluations and covers the param-0 case.
- None of the 5 listed guardrail positions changed.
- It is the only one of the three designs with measured bench reach.
- The designer openly reported the -24 pair, the missed s7421 finding and the s7454 drift.
reviews.summary:
Drop. The design sends a unit from a fallback it calls futile to its top objective (whose OC need is already filled) when its OC is 'pivotal' there: share >= 0.75 of a worst-case one-move threat. Every measure that looks past one round points the wrong way:
- **s7475 r2:** the fix reproduces the measured alternative exactly, and the gain flips from +4.00 at h1 to -3.00 [-9.10, 3.10] at h2.
- **s7454:** it redirects P2's Gamma from its own home objective to the centre, which measured -3.42 at h2.
- **s7421:** it misses the cluster's only finding confirmed at h2 (+14.83), whose value was denial.
- **Full game:** the only pair is -24, entirely from its 2 fires (M1 had 0 fires and so equals the base game). Neither fire matches the pattern in the evidence: one moved Allarus off the enemy home, the other moved Guard Beta off the centre.
- **Futility test:** it is a broader version of FAR_TRIP's skip, which (with OVERCOMMIT) lost 6.26 VP/game in this same Custodes mirror.

Limiting the design to its evidence (centre top only, no home or enemy-home fallback, a real flip at the top, rounds 2-3, army-based futility) would leave at most s7475 r2 among the findings. issues.situation: The redirect decides futility and pivotality with `lone_trip_oc`'s threat, which is enemy_oc + projected_enemy_oc. projected_enemy_oc (AIDecisionMaker.gd ~8830-8855) adds every enemy unit within one move (M+2"+CR) of an objective at full OC, with no 'nearest' weighting. So an enemy squad within one move of both the fallback and the top is counted in full at both, and the two-objective comparison double counts it. The codebase's RACE-1b halves exactly this case ('it can stand on only one'), and LONE-TRIP uses this upper bound only at a 2x ratio and only for fragile units. The thresholds are also asymmetric. A fallback is 'futile' at any share up to 1.0 (`<=`, so 18 vs 18 counts as futile, although equal OC is contested, i.e. denied, in 11e). A top is accepted at a share of only 0.75. Any top_share > fb_share passes, so a near-even trade such as fb 0.95 -> top 0.96 redirects on noise. Example: enemy squad E (10 OC) stands 7" from both the centre and obj_nml_1. Centre: plan 8 + unit 9 = 17 vs holders 8 + E 10 = 18, so futile. obj_nml_1: plan 12 vs holders 4 + E 10 = 14, so pivotal (21/14). The unit leaves the centre; if E then goes to nml_1, the centre would have been 17 vs 8 with the unit. The centre is within one move of the most enemy units, so it is the objective most often read 'futile'. The bias therefore pulls units off the centre, the opposite of every finding. One of the 2 bench fires is exactly this (Guard Beta -> obj_nml_2 instead of obj_center). The design's own 2-seed A/B at s7421 shows 18 planned OC denying the centre against a counted 25.
issues.proposed_change: Inside attack_move_redirect, compute both threats from ev.enemy_arrivals with RACE-1b weighting: enemy_oc plus, for each arrival with moves <= max(1, turns), its full OC if `nearest` and half otherwise (keep race_enemy_oc for multi-turn trips). Judge futility on the same scale as the top: futile only if fb_share < ATTACK_MOVE_MIN_SHARE, which also stops equal OC (contested) counting as futile. Require top_share >= fb_share + a margin (e.g. 0.25). s7475 (0.36 -> 1.35) and s7455 (0.43 -> 0.93) still redirect. Add unit tests for one enemy squad standing between the two objectives and for a near-even pair; neither should redirect.

reviews.fires_in_bench: About 1 [ATTACK_MOVE] line per game in the candidate seat (range roughly 0.5-2), so borderline for the >= 1.0 fix gate. Unvalidated: I did not run Godot. Basis: (a) the precondition, a unit whose top objective's OC need is filled and which falls to another objective, appears about 0.75 times per movement plan per side in 88 rollout logs on recent AI code (157 notes over 208 plans), i.e. about 3.8 per side per 5-round game. (b) A futile fallback plus (c) a pivotal top within 2 moves with share >= 0.75 should keep about a quarter of those. That matches the designer's 2 fires in 2 Custodes-mirror games (n = 2). Orks mirror: about 20 units per side and more contention, so probably more lines; but Ork melee-focused units (Beast Snagga Boyz, Stormboyz, characters) are converted to ATTACK after the line prints, so some fires there are no-ops. Custodes vs Orks: Custodes units rarely reach a 0.75 share against Ork threats; the Ork side fires sometimes. Direction: about 60% of the precondition events are top = flank -> fallback = centre, and both measured bench fires were home -> centre and centre -> flank. So most bench fires will likely fall outside the flank -> centre direction the findings support. Restricting the rule to that direction and excluding home fallbacks would probably push reach below 1.0.
reviews.strengths:
- Gating is clean. FIX_ATTACK_MOVE = 0 makes the lambda return {} before anything else, so the base `apply_capture_assignment(cand)` runs unchanged; the only other difference is a param-read record.
- The redirect sits at the end of pass 2's filter chain, so DIM-RETURNS, TOO-LATE, RACE-SKIP, LONE-TRIP and OBJ-ASSIGN-1 all run first, and the top is re-checked with the same skip lambdas.
- It keeps the top candidate's own action, so a Normal move stays Normal. For s7475 and s7455 the rollout override ran the same execution path (including the T7-23 blend), so the decision unit matches the measured branch B.
- Guards are conservative: top within 2 moves, not home, and it must outscore the fallback.
- The coordination note survives OBJ-EXPLAIN-1, and no debug log is removed.
- Cost is negligible: one evaluation per unit per plan, and the plan is built once per movement phase.
- The static ratchet passes on the patched file.
- It rebases onto V12 with a clean 3-way apply (plain `git apply` fails only on a context line), and it does not touch `_melee_chase_gate`, so it is compatible with waaagh_advance_charge.
- It is the only design whose code fires in the bench (1.0 per game measured).
- The test pins the fix on and erases the override, drives `_assign_units_to_objectives` with real evaluations, and fails on base for the right reason (runner not redirected, note absent).
- The report is candid that s7421 is not reached and that the bench pair came out negative.
reviews.summary: The code is tidy and correctly gated, and the main test is real: it pins the fix on and fails on base because the runner is not redirected. The core decision rule is miscalibrated, though. Futility and pivotality are judged from per-objective worst-case enemy OC, so one enemy squad within a move of both objectives is counted in full at each; RACE-1b halves exactly this case. The thresholds are also asymmetric: a fallback at up to 1.0 share (including equal OC, which is contested, i.e. denied, in 11e) counts as 'futile', while a top at 0.75 share is accepted. Together these bias the rule toward reading the centre as futile and pulling units off it, the opposite of the findings. The rule is symmetric, and both measured bench fires were outside the evidence (home -> centre, centre -> flank). On the evidence side, the positions it changes have null or negative horizon-2 numbers (s7475 -3.00; s7454 alternative -3.42), and it misses the only horizon-2-confirmed finding (s7421 +14.83, value from denial). Revise: weight the enemy threat by nearest objective, judge the fallback on the same 0.75 scale with a margin, exclude home fallbacks, restrict to the measured direction, and log after pass 2.5. Then re-run the protocol-v2 reach gate on all 3 fixtures; s7475 and s7455 still fire under these changes, but if reach drops below 1.0 per game, park it.

verdict.reasons:
Weighting: total = (evidence + generality + 2×full_game_safety + 2×bench_reach + code_quality) / 7. Reach counts only if what fires is the behaviour the evidence supports. None of the three is shippable as written. Narrow is the only design that becomes safe with small, specific edits. It is also the only one that keeps the measured execution at both h1-clear findings and applies cleanly on V12, so it can merge with the waaagh chase-gate code. It skips attack assignments and runs after pass 2.5.

What I verified myself (read-only; Godot not run; designer replay counts and test results were checked against the code, not re-run):
1. s7475 r2 and s7455 r2: charge targets are 21.4" and 20.4" away, beyond M8+12". No T7-23 blend applies, so all three designs reproduce branch B exactly.
2. s7421 r2: the blend does apply (Scout Squad Alpha is 17.4" away). Root's Normal move there is not the measured unblended Advance.
3. `_unit_alive_oc` excludes attached characters. The "lone 9 OC vs 11" trips really carry 11 OC, a tie under 14.02. Narrow's stated mechanism is wrong; its predicate is a planner proxy.
4. The bench Custodes list (5-model M6 Guard at 10 OC, unattached Blade Champions) does not contain the finding units (3-model M8 Guard at 9 OC with a leader). That explains 0 bench fires for narrow and root.
5. Patch check on base+V12: narrow clean, game 3-way clean, root conflicts.
6. Pass-3 `support_allowed` reads `planned_new_objs`, and the COORD-2 loop overwrites `coordination_note`. Both reviewer claims are true.

Why not game, despite reach: its fires are the wrong ones. Its threat model is biased against the centre, its one pair is negative, and its safe version loses its measured fires.

Why not root: the group-splitting is structural. Its only unique result (s7421) moves the unit out of range of both objectives. It conflicts with V12.

Evidence caveat. I counted the 24 measured Custodes positions where Move obj_center was the alternative to a side capture or flip. Mean +1.10 VP at h1: 3 clear, 2 harmful, 19 neutral. By round: +1.70 in round 2, +0.06 in round 3, which supports a round-2 gate. s7475 FADED at h2 (-3.00), and s7455 has no h2 check. The cluster's only CONFIRMED-H2 finding, s7421 (+14.83, denying the enemy's centre scoring), is handled by no design; it needs its own denial-trigger design. I expect the revised narrow design to be PARKED by the V2-1 fix gate. That outcome is acceptable: cheap, safe, and the code is kept.
